summary: No active lesson in learning.json names the fundamentals-analyst, and I have no graded calls, so today's call comes from the menu alone (menu_as_of 2026-11-24, 42 candidates, no flags except GRMN and ONC amended filings). The cleanest names are still the held quality core: VRSN (F9/9, gp_sector_pct 0.993), DPZ and CARG (both gp_sector_pct 1.0, F8). Outside the book, FTDR, TPR and AAPL have the best mix of a full or near-full F-score, high in-sector rank and cash flow above net income. RRC and CART are left out of the ranking because both are pending acquisitions (EQT all-stock; DoorDash at $65 per news_memory), so their prices follow the deal terms, not fundamentals.

rankings.why: The only held name passing all nine tests (fscore 9 of 9 computable). gp_sector_pct 0.993, gross_profitability 1.10, CFO $1,091.1M above net income $825.7M, and vol_252d 0.283 is among the calmest on the menu.
rankings.concerns: Technology label is fine. The FY ended 2025-12-31 and the data is 11 months old; the next 10-K is due around February. The stored thesis wording on a 'guidance raise' and 'top-ranked' status is the PM's to fix, not a fundamentals issue.

rankings.why: gp_sector_pct 1.0, gross_profitability 1.15, fscore 8 of 9, CFO $792.1M above net income $601.7M. It passes roa, margin and asset-turnover improvement.
rankings.concerns: Its only failed test is leverage_not_up. The top-of-sector rank is inflated by the Wholesale-Groceries SIC that files a restaurant franchisor under Consumer Staples. On absolute gross_profitability (1.15) it would still rank near the top of most sectors. Already the largest held name, so I would not add.

The PM has named it the first equity sell candidate, and nothing on the menu argues strongly against that. NYT (F9, gp_sector_pct 0.833) and MSM (F9, 0.823) were the next names out.

fscore_computable is 8: no_dilution is null and was scored 0, so F7 rests on eight tests (a recent listing). The Retail-Drug Stores SIC puts a pharmacy-services business in Consumer Staples; Health Care fits it better.

Sector label: an insurer and pharmacy-benefit business filed as Consumer Staples by its drug-store SIC, so its 0.903 in-sector rank is measured against grocers. Net income of $1,768M on $402B of revenue is thin, it fails no_dilution, and Medicare Advantage rule proposals are open per news_memory.
Sector label: an index and financial-data business filed as Industrials by its Business Services SIC, and it fails leverage_not_up. MCO has the same mislabel and also fails leverage_not_up.
Sector label: an industrial MRO distributor filed as Consumer Discretionary by its retail SIC. MSM (Wholesale-Industrial Machinery, also labeled Consumer Discretionary) has the same issue.
Sector label: a lighting and building-controls maker filed as Technology. Industrials fits better. A new up-to-$400M delayed-draw term loan was filed 11-20 (news_memory).
Sector label: an aerospace components maker filed as Materials by its metals SIC. Industrials fits better.

Net income of $17.9M on $1,000M of revenue is barely positive, so roa_positive and roa_improved hang on a thin margin, even though CFO ($135.0M) backs it. Communication fits a broadband equipment and software vendor only loosely.
Pending all-stock acquisition by EQT (news_memory). The fundamentals no longer drive the price.
Pending acquisition by DoorDash at $65 under DOJ review (news_memory), so the price follows the deal spread. The Industrials label is wrong for a grocery-delivery marketplace.
